ideas.risks: Could fail if the policy model permits law-by-law a.s. policy equivalence, private feedback not reconstructible from public prices, or internal state not representable by independent seeds. The result is only reward-vector equivalence, not pathwise equivalence.
ideas.summary: Write an exact finite-grid public-exogenous admissible policy model and prove the forward alignment lemma: every common Borel private-randomized policy induces law-independent Borel public-prefix kernels q_t(P_{1:t}) preserving all expected reward coordinates L_theta. Include persistent internal state and delayed trade feedback explicitly.
ideas.title: Borel Policy Alignment
ideas.why_promising: This is the main remaining gap between the accepted completed-L-infinity no-gap theorem and a theorem for the intended original policy class. It is local, finite-horizon, and should be checkable by induction plus Fubini.

ideas.risks: Null sets under the mixture prefix law may obscure the equality if the dominating measure is chosen poorly. Need handle zero-density prefixes and verify finite-G measurability cleanly.
ideas.summary: Prove rigorously that the density-form support formula under payoff-measure domination equals the conditional Bayes envelope defining Psi_{G,F}. Work with finite F, prior pi, measures nu_{t,a}=sum_theta pi_theta mu^theta_{t,a}, and compare Radon-Nikodym densities using both lambda_t and the mixture prefix law.
ideas.title: Density Psi Identification
ideas.why_promising: The iteration 12 solver asserts this as a concrete new closure step. A short proof would make the infinite-class no-gap statement use the same Psi notation as the finite-class theorem.

ideas.risks: A counterexample may require pathological definitions already excluded by a careful policy model. Explorers should distinguish genuine failures from failures caused by changing the model.
ideas.summary: Stress-test the claimed original-policy alignment by varying assumptions one at a time: private/censored feedback, action-dependent prices, law-correlated randomization, policies defined only up to law-specific null sets, or same-period trading. For each variant, either produce a counterexample or explain why the original assumptions exclude it.
ideas.title: Alignment Failure Modes
ideas.why_promising: This will prevent the final theorem from silently relying on hidden assumptions. It can also clarify exactly why public exogeneity and common Borel policies are essential.

ideas.risks: Naive block repetition collapses because the fixed comparator sees expected mixtures, and one reveal can teach the global type. Need avoid these known failures explicitly.
ideas.summary: Design multi-scale or limited-leakage finite-horizon classes that accumulate many hidden-terminal Bayes gaps while satisfying a tail envelope B(h), aiming to match or approach the upper rate sqrt(T H)+T B(H). Candidate designs: independent hidden bits at separated quote levels, terminal observations that reveal only noisy summaries, or Fano-style families with small KL across public prefixes.
ideas.title: Power-Tail Lower Rates
ideas.why_promising: Matching lower rates are the largest open quantitative issue. The accepted finite-grid Bayes value formula gives a way to compute or certify lower bounds for carefully designed finite classes.

ideas.risks: Running many H-window algorithms may incur too much overhead, and delayed feedback timing may break standard model-selection arguments. Comparator-gap terms may not combine in a clean oracle inequality.
ideas.summary: Investigate an adaptive truncation algorithm competing with the best truncation horizon H in hindsight, targeting an oracle bound like inf_H {sqrt(T H log K)+T/K+delta_T(H)} plus logarithmic overhead. Try dyadic H, meta-Hedge over base delayed-expert algorithms, and careful accounting of when each base algorithm receives feedback.
ideas.title: Adaptive Truncation
ideas.why_promising: The current sufficient theorem requires choosing H from a known tail profile. Adaptivity would strengthen the upper theory and may reveal whether the present rates are proof artifacts.

ideas.risks: May either reduce to domination/TV separability or to easy identifiability. Need avoid claiming weak/Feller continuity alone, which is already known insufficient.
ideas.summary: Search for natural no-gap hypotheses beyond payoff-measure domination: finite-time Borel identifiability, dominated-on-fibers after public labels, analytic parametric families with measurable decoders, or direct compactness of the attainable reward set. State checkable sufficient conditions and test them against uncountable Dirac examples.
ideas.title: Natural Infinite-Class No-Gap
ideas.why_promising: Common payoff-measure domination excludes many deterministic or singular classes. A broader no-gap theorem would make the Bayes-value characterization substantially more useful.

ideas.risks: Known examples are pathological non-Borel label constructions. A natural Borel gap may not exist under standard public-prefix policies, or may require a more subtle descriptive-set-theoretic setup.
ideas.summary: Try to construct a Borel, nondominated, non-identifiable infinite class where every finite subclass has small grid minimax value but the full Borel-policy class has linear value. Alternatively, prove that broad Borel/analytic regularity plus finite-grid public exogeneity rules out such gaps under an appropriate measurability condition.
ideas.title: Borel Infinite-Class Gap
ideas.why_promising: This directly probes whether the product-closure/no-gap assumptions are merely technical or hide real statistical obstructions beyond non-Borel pathologies.

ideas.risks: The issue is outside the main horizon-aware minimax theorem and could distract unless scoped narrowly. Doubling or randomized horizon schedules might weaken the obstruction.
ideas.summary: Formalize the candidate anytime known-law obstruction using super-growing deterministic blocks with two possible deadlines. Prove or refute that a single horizon-free policy for a known infinite exogenous sequence can suffer linear regret along one deadline subsequence despite each finite horizon being oracle-learnable.
ideas.title: Anytime Known-Law Boundary
ideas.why_promising: The known-law oracle lemma is horizon-aware. Settling the anytime boundary would sharpen the model taxonomy and prevent overclaiming fixed-law learnability.
